Check that the test asserts document scrollWidth equals the viewport width of 320.
Run the same test at 1280px to confirm the two-column layout still applies.

K-015941.example: At viewport 320x640, document.documentElement.scrollWidth must be 320, so no field overflows. At 1280px the grid must have two columns, so getComputedStyle(grid).gridTemplateColumns has two track values.
K-015941.check: grep prints a line containing '@media (min-width: 480px)'; both Playwright runs print '1 passed'. A failure prints 'Expected: 320 Received: 412'.
traps: Do not test only at desktop width; the 320px case is where stacked fields overflow.
Do not assume a breakpoint works; compare the media query value with the width the test uses.
Do not use fixed pixel widths on inputs, since they push the row wider than the viewport.

steps.do: Confirm the button CSS sets a minimum height of 44px.
Run the Playwright test that measures the button's bounding box at a 390px viewport.
Lint the button component so its props and types stay valid.

K-015942.example: The test calls button.boundingBox() at a 390px viewport and expects height to be at least 44. A value of 36 means the CSS needs min-height: 44px.
K-015942.check: grep prints 'min-height: 44px'; Playwright prints '1 passed'; eslint exits 0 with no output. A failure prints 'Expected >= 44 Received 36'.
traps: Do not measure with a hidden or disabled button; check it in its enabled state.
Do not trust the CSS value alone; check the measured boundingBox, since padding or overflow can change the result.
Do not confuse font-size with height; a 16px label can still sit inside a 36px box.

steps.do: Run the Vitest suite for the signup schema.
Count the safeParse assertions in the test file to confirm each rule has a case.
Type-check the schema and the zodResolver wiring.

K-015943.example: The schema with password min(8) must reject 'abc1234' (7 characters) and accept 'abcd1234' (8 characters). The count of safeParse should be at least 6 for six rules.
K-015943.check: Vitest prints 'Tests 6 passed (6)'; grep prints 6 or more; tsc prints nothing and exits 0.
traps: Do not test only valid input; each rule needs at least one rejected value.
Do not test only one side of a boundary; check one value just below the limit and one value at the limit.
Do not skip the z.infer type; a type mismatch between schema and form shows up only in tsc.

steps.do: Confirm the test waits for the error with a 200ms timeout.
Run the Jest test that types an invalid email and blurs the field.
steps.cmd: npx jest src/components/SignupForm.test.tsx --testNamePattern 'shows error on blur'

steps.do: Run the Jest test that checks the submit button is disabled until all fields are valid.

K-015944.example: After typing 'ada@' and blurring the email field, waitFor must find 'Enter a valid email address.' within 200ms. The submit button must have the disabled attribute until all fields pass validation.
K-015944.check: grep prints a line with 'timeout: 200'; both Jest runs print 'Tests: 1 passed, 1 total'. A slow error prints 'Timed out in waitFor after 200ms'.
traps: Do not query the error synchronously after blur; React Hook Form validates asynchronously, so use waitFor or findByText.
Do not raise the timeout above 200 to make a slow test pass; fix the delay instead.
Do not check only the error text; also assert the disabled state on submit.

steps.do: Count the htmlFor attributes in the FormField component.
Count the id attributes on the input in the same component.
Lint the component with zero warnings allowed to enforce jsx-a11y rules.
Type-check the project to confirm the props type matches every caller.

K-015945.example: FormField takes a name prop and renders <label htmlFor={id}> with <input id={id}>, so both counts are 1. The eslint run must exit 0 with no warnings.
K-015945.check: Both grep counts print 1; eslint prints nothing and exits 0; tsc prints nothing and exits 0. Any warning prints a line naming a jsx-a11y rule with a count.
traps: Do not add eslint-disable comments to silence jsx-a11y; fix the markup instead.
Do not use placeholder text as the only label, because it disappears when the user types.
Do not hardcode id values; use React's useId hook so repeated fields on one page stay unique.

steps.do: Search the source root for manual formatters and hard-coded format strings.
Count the manual formatter sites per file so the plan has a number.
Plan to replace each date with Text(date, format: .dateTime) and each price with Text(value, format: .currency(code:)).
Count how many test locale identifiers appear in the Tests folder, expecting at least 3 for en_US, de_DE, and ar_SA.

K-015946.example: rg -c reports 4 manual formatter sites, 3 in OrderRow.swift and 1 in PriceLabel.swift. Each becomes Text(value, format: .currency(code: "EUR")), so the device locale controls the separators.
K-015946.check: The rg -c output lists each file's integer, the plan's total equals the sum of 4 in the example, and the locale count is 3 or more.
traps: A small model keeps DateFormatter with a fixed dateFormat string, which ignores the user's locale. Setting locale to en_US_POSIX in a user-facing formatter is also wrong.

steps.do: Read the theme file to see the breakpoint scale in use.
Search the CSS for a Tailwind v4 @theme block that might override breakpoints.
Count how many files already use the md: prefix to match the team's habit.
Write the plan as: nav collapses below md, which is 48rem or 768px, and shows inline from md up.

K-015947.example: The project has no custom screens, so the default md breakpoint (48rem, 768px) is the switch point. Four files already use md:, so the plan keeps md and does not add a new breakpoint.
K-015947.check: The cat output lists no custom screens, rg -c prints nonzero counts for md:, and the plan names 768px as the collapse width.
traps: Small models often pick sm (640px) because it appears first in the scale. Tailwind is mobile-first, so md:hidden hides the element from 768px up, not below it. Do not add a custom breakpoint when a d…

steps.do: Find the file that contains the nav element.
Confirm the candidate component file exists at its path.
Count the href links in that file, excluding the footer.
If the count is 5 or fewer, plan inline links at md. If it is 6 or more, plan a menu toggle below lg, which is 1024px.

K-015948.example: Navbar.tsx has 7 href matches, so the plan uses a menu toggle below lg (1024px) and inline links from lg up. The count includes the logo link, so the real item count is 6, which still means a menu toggle.
K-015948.check: rg prints the nav file path, test exits with status 0, and grep -c prints a number that you compare to the 5-item rule.
traps: Small models count links inside the hidden mobile menu too, which doubles the number. Count only the primary nav items, not footer or duplicate links. Plan the threshold from the count, not from a gu…

steps.do: Check whether the project already uses min-h-11 on interactive elements.
Confirm that Tailwind's spacing 11 equals 2.75rem, which is 44px at the default 4px base.
Plan each mobile link as a block with py-3 px-4 min-h-11 w-full so the hit area covers the row.
Record that the minimum target is 44px in both height and width.

K-015949.example: A mobile link uses py-3 px-4 min-h-11 w-full, which gives a row at least 44px tall and full width. The node check prints 44, which matches 11 times 4.
K-015949.check: node prints 44, and the plan lists min-h-11 with w-full on each mobile link.
traps: Small models read min-h-11 as 11px. In Tailwind the number is a spacing step, so 11 means 2.75rem, which is 44px. Setting only a height class leaves the width too small, so add w-full to the link.

steps.do: List the component folder to find the nav container file.
Find the lines that set flex classes in the nav file.
Plan the base classes as flex flex-col gap-4 with no prefix, since unprefixed classes apply to all widths.
Plan md:flex-row and md:items-center as the override from 768px up.

K-015950.example: The base class is flex flex-col gap-4, and md:flex-row md:items-center switches to a row at 768px. The unprefixed class covers phones, so no max-width variant is needed.
K-015950.check: ls lists Navbar.tsx, rg prints the line numbers of the flex classes, and the plan pairs each base class with one md: override.
traps: Small models write md:flex-col and md:flex-row together, which conflicts and makes the result depend on order. Put the mobile value unprefixed and the desktop value with md:. Do not use max-md on eve…

steps.do: Check whether a Playwright config file exists in the project root.
Read the configured projects to see which viewport sizes are already set.
Plan three test widths: 375px for a phone, 768px for the md switch, and 1280px for desktop.
Count the planned widths to confirm there are three.

K-015951.example: The test plan uses 375px, 768px and 1280px, which cover the phone layout, the md switch and the desktop layout. The node count prints 3, so all three widths are listed.
K-015951.check: ls prints the config path, cat shows the viewport settings, and node prints 3.
traps: Small models test only desktop width and miss the mobile menu entirely. Use 768px as the exact switch width, not 640px. Device emulation alone is not enough, so set explicit pixel widths for each cas…

steps.do: Create the trigger as a button element with type set to button, not a div, so keyboard activation works by default.
Add aria-haspopup and aria-expanded bound to the open state variable.
Apply focus-visible:outline-none, focus-visible:ring-2, and focus-visible:ring-sky-600 together, plus min-h-11 and min-w-11 for the 44px target.
Rebuild the stylesheet so the new focus-visible classes are generated in the output file.
Confirm the generated CSS contains the focus-visible ring rule.

K-015952.example: <button type='button' aria-haspopup='menu' aria-expanded={open} className='min-h-11 min-w-11 rounded-md px-3 focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-sky-600'>Account</button> is the trigger, and the rebuild writes its classes to dist/output.css.
K-015952.check: The CLI finishes with no error text, and rg prints at least one line containing focus-visible:ring-2 from dist/output.css.
traps: Using focus-visible:outline-none with no ring leaves keyboard users with no visible focus. Always pair it with a ring or border change.
Small models use focus: instead of focus-visible:, which shows the ring on mouse clicks too.

steps.do: Render the panel only when open, using conditional rendering instead of the hidden class, so closed items leave the accessibility tree.
Give each item role=menuitem and tabIndex of -1, then move focus to the first item when the panel opens.
Confirm the component binds aria-expanded to the same state that controls the panel.
Type-check the component so a missing prop or wrong type fails now.

K-015953.example:
The panel renders as {open &&
    ...
}, and the first li child receives focus in an effect after open becomes true. The grep prints src/components/Menu.tsx:18 with aria-expanded={open}, which matches the panel state.
K-015953.check: rg prints the aria-expanded line that uses the same variable as the panel condition, and tsc exits with code 0 and no output.
traps: Small models hide the panel with the hidden class but keep the items focusable, so Tab reaches invisible links. Remove closed items from rendering or set tabIndex to -1.
Forgetting to move focus into the panel on open leaves keyboard users on the trigger with no way to reach the items.

steps.do: Start the dev server on port 5173 and open the page that contains the menu.
Run the axe CLI against the menu page URL and record the violation count.
Run the same scan limited to WCAG 2.1 AA tags to match the target level.
Fix each violation by its rule id, then rerun the scan until the count is zero.

K-015954.example: The first scan reports 2 violations, aria-allowed-attr on the trigger and color-contrast on the item text. After adding the correct aria attribute and changing text-slate-400 to text-slate-600, the rerun reports 0 violations and exits with code 0.
K-015954.check: The axe output lists zero violations and the command exits with code 0.
traps: Small models treat an empty axe run as proof of full accessibility. Axe does not test keyboard behavior or focus order.
Running axe while the menu is closed skips the items. Open the menu first or use a test that opens it.

steps.do: Write the budgets into the plan file: spinner shown within 200ms, 5 skeleton rows, and 44pt minimum tap height.
Search for existing minHeight settings so the 44pt rule matches the project.
Confirm the plan file contains the 200ms budget.

K-015955.example: The plan states a spinner appears within 200ms and that each row has a minimum height of 44pt. The rg search finds no conflicting minHeight values in the project.
K-015955.check: The rg command on PLAN-menu-loading.md prints one line containing 200ms, and the minHeight search lists existing values, or nothing if there are none.
traps: Do not write vague goals like fast or smooth, because a small model cannot test them.
Do not choose a tap height below 44pt, which is Apple's minimum for touch targets.
Do not forget the time budget, since the verify stage checks timing against it.

steps.do: Search the repo for existing aria-expanded attributes to match the team's pattern.
Check whether the components already keep open state with useState.
Check whether a screen-reader-only label class is already in use.
Check that the Playwright runner is installed and print its version number.
Check existing touch-target sizes for 44px (Tailwind h-11 or w-11) to match the team's minimum.
Plan a button with aria-expanded set to the open boolean, aria-controls pointing to the menu id, class md:hidden, and an sr-only text label.

K-015956.example: The toggle uses aria-expanded={open} and aria-controls='mobile-menu' with class md:hidden h-11 w-11, so it appears only below 768px and meets the 44px touch target. The sr-only label gives screen readers a name for the button.
K-015956.check: rg prints the existing aria-expanded lines or none, the useState grep lists the open state, npx playwright --version prints a version number, the h-11 grep shows 44px touch-target matches or none, and the plan names the menu id used in aria-controls.
traps: Small models set aria-expanded to the string 'true' or leave it out. Pass the boolean open state so React renders it correctly. Hiding the button with a CSS display rule without md:hidden leaves it v…

steps.do: Set the minimum hit area to 44px with min-h-11 and min-w-11 on the trigger and on every item.
Find the focus ring classes already used in components so the new focus style matches them.
Set the focus ring to ring-2 with ring-offset-2, using a ring color with at least 3:1 contrast against the background.
Find the sizing classes already used in components so the new menu matches them.
Read the top of the component file so you know where the sizing comment goes.
Write the chosen values into a short comment at the top of the component file.

K-015957.example: The trigger uses min-h-11 and min-w-11 for a 44px target, and each item uses py-2.5 and px-4 for a row height of at least 44px. The focus ring is ring-2 ring-sky-600 ring-offset-2 on a white background, which is above 3:1 against white.
K-015957.check: rg prints lines that contain min-h- or nothing if none exist, and the trigger class string contains min-h-11 and min-w-11. The head output shows the file's first 5 lines.
traps: Small models use min-h-8 (32px), which fails the 44px target. min-h-11 equals 2.75rem, or 44px at the default 16px root size.
A ring in ring-gray-200 on white is too faint to meet the 3:1 non-text contrast rule.

steps.do: Start the dev server in its own terminal so Playwright has a page to load.
Create the empty keyboard spec file.
Write a test that focuses the trigger, presses Enter, and expects the first menuitem to have focus.
Add a step that presses ArrowDown twice and expects the third item to be focused.
Add a step that presses Escape and expects the menu to be hidden within 200ms and focus to return to the trigger.
Run the keyboard spec file and read the pass count.

K-015958.example: The test calls page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Account' }).press('Enter'), then expects page.getByRole('menuitem').first() to be focused. After Escape, expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Account' })).toBeFocused() passes within the 200ms timeout.
K-015958.check: The run prints 1 passed with no failed tests, and the exit code is 0.
traps: Small models test only with mouse clicks and skip Escape and Tab, so focus traps stay hidden. Add a keyboard test for each state.
Forgetting to start the dev server makes Playwright fail with connection refused, which looks like a menu bug but is a setup error.

steps.do: Check the installed Swift toolchain version.
Locate the xcodebuild binary used for the build and test steps.
Create the plan file if it does not exist yet.
Write the 10 second request timeout and the retry button rule into the plan.
steps.cmd: sed -i '$a Failure: after 10s show failed state with Retry button, min 44pt tap height' PLAN-menu-loading.md

steps.do: Count the lines in the plan that contain the 10s timeout; the count must be 1.

K-015959.example: The toolchain prints Swift version 6.1, and the plan records a 10s timeout that shows a Retry button at 44pt height. The rg -c command prints 1.
K-015959.check: swift --version prints a line starting with Swift version, and rg -c prints the number 1 for the plan file.
traps: Do not plan a timeout without a number, because a small model cannot verify 'a while'.
Do not assume a Swift version; read it from swift --version output.
Do not forget the retry action, since users need a way out of the failed state.

steps.do: List each field name and its input type in a table.
Set a numeric length limit for each text field, such as 1 to 80 characters for name.
Search existing code for length and pattern rules to reuse matching limits.
Set the email maximum to 254 characters and the password minimum to 12 characters.
Count the lines in the plan to confirm every field has a rule.

K-015960.example: Name is 1 to 80 characters, email is at most 254 characters, and password is at least 12 characters. The plan records each limit in PLAN.md, which then shows at least 5 lines.
K-015960.check: rg prints matches or nothing, and wc -l PLAN.md reports at least 5 lines with a rule for every field.
traps: Leaving a field without a rule.
Choosing a password minimum without checking the project policy.
Deciding when validation runs without writing it down in the plan.

steps.do: Check whether the project already uses the native dialog element and showModal.
Decide that Escape closes the modal and focus returns to the button that opened it.
Decide the close button is at least 44px by 44px.
Decide the open and close transition lasts 200ms or less.
Confirm the Playwright version so keyboard tests can run later.

K-015961.example: The plan uses a native dialog element opened with showModal, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the Open profile button. The close button is 44px by 44px and the fade lasts 200ms.
K-015961.check: rg prints matches or nothing, npx playwright --version prints a version number, and the plan states 44px and 200ms.
traps: Using a plain div with role dialog and no focus trap.
Setting the close target below 44px.
Forgetting that focus must return to the trigger after the modal closes.

steps.do: Decide each input gets aria-invalid set to true only when it has an error.
Decide each error message links to its input with aria-describedby.
Decide the error text reaches a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 on its background.
Check existing color settings in the global stylesheet.
Decide a summary with role alert lists all errors at the top of the modal.
Count the decisions recorded in PLAN.md.

K-015962.example: The email input sets aria-invalid to true and aria-describedby to email-error. The error text uses #b00020 on white, which is about 7:1, above the 4.5:1 target.
K-015962.check: rg prints color lines or nothing, wc -l PLAN.md reports at least 5 lines, and the plan states the 4.5:1 target.
traps: Using red text alone to show errors.
Forgetting aria-describedby, so screen readers skip the message.
Setting aria-invalid on fields the user has not touched yet.

steps.do: Check that a Playwright config file exists.
List the existing Playwright tests to see the current count.
Write one test case for each rule: empty name, name over 80 characters, bad email, short password, and a valid submit.
Set the plan to exactly 5 test cases and check the count against the rules.
Confirm a check script exists in package.json.

K-015963.example: The plan lists five cases: empty name, name over 80 characters, bad email, password under 12 characters, and a valid submit. After the spec file exists, npx playwright test --list reports Total: 5 tests in 1 file.
K-015963.check: test -f exits with status 0 when the config exists, npx playwright test --list prints a Total line such as Total: 5 tests in 1 file, and the plan lists 5 cases.
traps: Writing tests that only cover the happy path.
Skipping the count, so coverage stays unknown.
Assuming a Playwright config exists without testing for it.

steps.do: Confirm the styles folder exists and see what it holds.
Check whether any font-size tokens are already declared.
Decide a base of 1rem with a 1.25 ratio, giving 1rem, 1.25rem, and 1.5625rem.
Write --text-base, --text-lg, and --text-xl under :root in src/styles/tokens.css.
Confirm the token name --text-base appears once in the styles folder.
Confirm main.ts imports the tokens file exactly once.

K-015964.example: Declaring --text-base: 1rem and --text-lg: 1.25rem in tokens.css, then importing it once in main.ts, gives every onboarding component the same sizes. A component then uses font-size: var(--text-lg) instead of a px literal.
K-015964.check: rg -c prints src/styles/tokens.css:1 for --text-base, and the import search prints one line in src/main.ts.
traps: Using px for the tokens blocks users who scale their browser font size.
Declaring tokens inside each component duplicates them.
Forgetting to import tokens.css leaves every var() undefined.

steps.do: List the color declarations in the onboarding styles.
Create scripts/contrast.mjs that prints the WCAG ratio and PASS or FAIL, then run it on the candidate text and background pair.
Note that body text needs 4.5:1 and text at 24px regular or larger needs 3:1.
Run the same script on each hover, focus, and disabled color pair.
Run the axe audit on the onboarding route once the dev server is up.

K-015965.example: Running the script with #767676 on #ffffff prints 4.54:1 PASS, which clears 4.5:1 for body text. The same script with #888888 on #ffffff prints 3.54:1 FAIL, so that gray only works for text at 24px regular or larger.
K-015965.check: The script prints a ratio with PASS or FAIL for each pair, and axe reports zero color-contrast violations.
traps: Checking the final text color without its background token gives a false pass.
Applying the 3:1 large-text rule to 16px body copy is a common error.
Hover and focus states need their own ratio checks.

steps.do: List the button elements in the onboarding components.
List the min-height declarations already in the onboarding styles.
Set --space-2 to 0.5rem, --space-4 to 1rem, and --space-6 to 1.5rem on a 4px base in tokens.css.
Set --tap-min to 44px in tokens.css and plan to apply it as min-height on each interactive control.
Run the Playwright spec that measures each control's bounding box height.

K-015966.example: A Next button with padding 0.75rem 1.5rem and 1rem text renders about 48px tall, which passes 44px. An icon-only close button at 28px needs min-height set to var(--tap-min) to reach 44px.
K-015966.check: Playwright prints 1 passed, and every measured control has a height of 44px or more.
traps: Measuring the visible icon instead of the clickable area gives a false pass.
Hard-coding 44px in several files lets the values drift apart.
Mixing 2.75rem and 44px for the same target makes the tokens inconsistent.

steps.do: Confirm which Vue version is installed so v-bind in style and useCssVars are available.
Check whether a tokens file already exists under src.
Decide that tokens.css is the single source and that JavaScript reads it only through a useTokens composable.
List the planned files: src/styles/tokens.css, src/composables/useTokens.ts, and each onboarding .vue file that uses them.
Confirm the project type-checks before any token change is made.

K-015967.example: npm ls vue prints vue@3.5.x, so v-bind() in style blocks and useCssVars from vue are available. Keeping values in tokens.css and reading them in useTokens.ts with getComputedStyle means JavaScript and CSS never hold separate copies.
K-015967.check: npm ls vue prints one vue@3.x line, find lists src/styles/tokens.css, and vue-tsc exits with no errors.
traps: Vue 2 APIs such as Vue.set do not exist in Vue 3 script setup.
useCssVars sets variables on the component root element, not on :root.
A second JavaScript copy of the colors drifts from the CSS over time.

steps.do: List the heading elements used in the onboarding components.
Confirm each onboarding view has exactly one h1 by counting them.
Map the title role to --text-xl, the body role to --text-base, and the caption role to --text-sm in the plan file.
Set the body copy max-width to between 45ch and 75ch in the plan.
Run eslint on the onboarding folder and confirm it reports no errors.

K-015968.example: OnboardingView.vue has one h1 styled with --text-xl at 1.5625rem, and its paragraph uses --text-base at 1rem with max-width 65ch. Captions use --text-sm at 0.875rem.
K-015968.check: rg -c prints src/views/OnboardingView.vue:1 with a count of 1, and eslint exits with no errors.
traps: Skipping heading levels, such as h1 straight to h3, breaks the document outline.
Mapping roles to raw px values defeats the purpose of the tokens.
Setting body line length in px ignores the user's font size, so use ch instead.

steps.do: Create the output folder before building.
Compile and minify the Tailwind stylesheet from the form input file.
Count the bytes in the compiled file.
Pass if the byte count is 15000 or less, otherwise remove unused arbitrary values such as w-[37.5rem] from the form components and rebuild.

K-015969.example: The stat command prints 11842, which is under the 15000 byte budget, so the check passes. If it prints 18210, remove arbitrary values from the form components and run the build again.
K-015969.check: stat prints a number at or below 15000, and the build prints a Done in line with no errors.
traps: Do not skip --minify, because the unminified file is much larger and fails the budget for the wrong reason.
Compare the size of dist/form.css, not the size of the input file src/styles.css.

steps.do: Start the site so the form page loads at http://localhost:3000/contact.
Create the reports folder for the Lighthouse output.
Run Lighthouse on the form page with only the performance category, writing JSON to a file.
Read the performance score from the JSON file.
Pass only if the score is 0.90 or higher.

K-015970.example: jq prints 0.93 for the contact form page, which is above 0.90, so the check passes. If it prints 0.78, open the largest-contentful-paint audit in form.json and fix that first.
K-015970.check: jq prints a number of 0.90 or higher, and reports/form.json exists.
traps: The JSON score is between 0 and 1, so 93 is wrong and 0.93 is right.
Rebuild before testing, because a stale build gives an old score.

steps.do: Create the reports folder.
Run Lighthouse on the form page and audit only cumulative layout shift.
Read the numeric value of the layout shift audit.
Fail the form if the value is above 0.1, and reserve height for error text so fields do not jump.

K-015971.example: jq prints 0.04, which is under 0.1, so the form passes. If it prints 0.25, give the error message container a fixed height such as min-h-5 so the layout does not shift.
K-015971.check: jq prints a number at or below 0.1.
traps: Layout shift is unitless, so do not convert it to milliseconds.
Lighthouse only measures page load, so a shift caused by validation needs a separate Playwright test.

steps.do: Confirm the latency spec file exists at the expected path.
Install the Chromium browser that Playwright uses.
Run the typing latency test file.
Fail the card if the test reports any keystroke above 200ms.

K-015972.example: The run reports 1 passed with a maximum keystroke time of 38ms, which is under the 200ms limit. If it reports a keystroke at 240ms, move regex validation from each keystroke to the blur event.
K-015972.check: The playwright output ends with 1 passed and has no failed lines.
traps: The spec must time typing, not page load.
Do not replace the 200ms assertion with a fixed waitForTimeout call.

steps.do: List the form files that use peer-invalid classes.
Build the stylesheet from the input file.
Check that the compiled CSS contains the peer-invalid rule.
If the count is 0, add @source "../src/components/form" to src/styles.css and build again.

K-015973.example: rg lists src/components/form/Input.tsx, and grep prints 1, so the rule compiled. If grep prints 0, add the @source line to src/styles.css and build again.
K-015973.check: grep prints 1 or more, and rg lists at least one .tsx file.
traps: Tailwind only generates classes from files it scans, so a missing @source line drops rules without an error.
Minified CSS is one line, so grep -c counts lines, and a count of 1 means the rule was found.

steps.do: List the source folders two levels deep.
Find existing dialog and form usage.
